items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: He played this -- and that was why I took my ambition as to be a great musician. And I've always honored Eubie, because I know that he was behind it all.

ctx.x: So -- but, in this place, they had a fellow, a man, called Madison Reed. Madison Reed had the show in there. And he had in that show -- his piano player was a man called Eubie Blake. And Eubie Blake -- and he had a singer called Mary Stafford. And I don't know what was the names of some other people, but he did most of it. He was one of the greatest entertainers of that day, this Madison Reed was, see.

So, I used to go to the window, on the outside, and stand on a beer box or something like that and look in the window. And when I looked in the window, I could see Eubie in there playing. And there was a song come out about that time called, "I Wonder Where My Easy Rider's Gone". And then, Madison did a piece called, "Black Prince". And when Eubie used to play these things, and I thought he was the greatest. He was very good. He was very good. He played this -- and that was why I took my ambition as to be a great…
And now, I had my inspiration from Williams and Walker.
